summary: The plain push assumes over 95% of reads come from cache. The final tests that against a simulation and an hour of real Wikipedia traffic, finds 20–40% more likely, and sizes the database to work with no cache at all. Every decision says what would flip it, it works out that guessing 7-character links finds about 736k live links a day, and it shows where the design breaks at 100k requests a second. Its own check passes 43/43. (A first run got stuck planning a rewrite instead of improving the document; we fixed the method's wording and re-ran.)
